reason: The cited evidence shows that redox cycling can reversibly restructure Pd in a quinary catalyst (E2) and that Cu-containing catalysts can oxidize at low temperatures (implied by the research question), but no evidence is provided that redox cycling creates Cu-rich domains, that isolated Pd sites resist poisoning, or that such treatment works at the low temperatures (150–200 °C) proposed. E1 and E3 are about Pd oxidation and HEA formation at higher temperatures and do not support the specific segregation or poisoning-resistance claims.
premises: Redox cycling induces surface segregation in high-entropy alloys
Isolated Pd sites resist poisoning by NO and H2O
Sacrificial oxidation of base metals encapsulates Pd and prevents poisoning
Redox treatment can be performed at ≤200 °C without sintering
